abstract: Control of magnetization reversal is crucial for spintronic memory and logic devices. Previous studies on two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) magnets have largely treated magnetic regions in isolation, leaving the roles of step boundaries comparatively unexplored. Here, we investigate step-boundary-triggered nonlocal modulation of magnetization reversal in multi-stepped Fe3GaTe2 using Kerr microscopy, Lorentz transmission electron microscopy, and micromagnetic simulations. Our results indicate that step boundaries can serve as preferential sites for premature nucleation, giving rise to two distinct regimes. In Type I, reversal initiated in a thicker region propagates rapidly across the step boundary, reducing the coercivity of an adjacent thinner region by up to 59.3%. In Type II, stripe domains originating from the thicker region progressively enter the thinner region, shifting its critical switching field polarity and transforming its hysteresis loop from square to slanted, accompanied by a transition in the dominant reversal mode from rapid domain-wall motion to stripe domain growth. Similar behavior in Fe3GeTe2 suggests that step-boundary-mediated modulation may occur more broadly in layered van der Waals ferromagnets. Our findings highlight step engineering as a potential non-invasive strategy for designing efficient and thermally stable vdW spintronic devices.

title: Cooperative Agostic‐Type C─H···Cu, Quadrupolar Cu···CO 2 , and C─H···O/π Interactions in an Ultra‐Microporous MOF Enable One‐Step Methane Purification From Quaternary C 3 H 8 /C 2 H 6 /CO 2 /CH 4
abstract: ABSTRACT While agostic‐type C─H···metal σ‐interactions are central to organometallic catalysis, their role in gas separation remains elusive. In this study, a robust phosphine‐functionalized ultra‐microporous Cu(I/II)‐organic framework, LIFM‐XYY‐15, featuring open metal sites (OMSs) and rich aromatic pore walls, is designed to enable one‐step CH 4 purification from a quaternary C 3 H 8 /C 2 H 6 /CO 2 /CH 4 mixture. Notably, LIFM‐XYY‐15 exhibits much higher C 3 H 8 /C 2 H 6 /CO 2 uptakes than CH 4 , showing C 3 H 8 /CH 4 , C 2 H 6 /CH 4 , and CO 2 /CH 4 uptake ratios of 2.46, 2.30, and 3.92 at 298 K and 1 bar, respectively, which are significantly raised to 12.18, 8.59, and 9.89 at 0.1 bar. The separation potentials (∆ q ) reach 22.12 (C 3 H 8 /CH 4 ), 20.34 (C 2 H 6 /CH 4 ), and 43.69 (CO 2 /CH 4 ) cm 3 cm −3 at 298 K and 1 bar, demonstrating excellent CH 4 purification ability from the quaternary mixture. Breakthrough experiments confirm the delivery of high‐purity CH 4 (≥99.9%) with a productivity of 1.39 mol L −1 with excellent recyclability. The in situ single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction (SCXRD), in situ FT‐IR spectroscopy, and molecular simulations reveal that the exceptional selectivity arises from the synergistic interplay of agostic‐type C─H···Cu, quadrupole‐electrostatic Cu···‐CO 2 , and alkane C─H···O/π interactions, which collectively reinforce the affinity for C 2 –C 3 hydrocarbons and CO 2 while disfavoring CH 4 . This work discloses a crucial role of agostic‐type interactions as a powerful yet underexplored design principle for selective hydrocarbon separations.

title: Intrinsically flexible inorganic piezoelectric subnanowire enables wireless wearable bioelectronics for non-invasive multimodal human-machine interfacing
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Piezoelectric electronic skin (PE-skin) offers a significant advantage in detecting minute forces, making it highly promising for human-computer interaction in health management and medical rehabilitation. However, PE-skin often faces challenges in real-time, wireless transmission of sensing data, which can compromise both data accuracy and user comfort. Here, we report the synthesis of an inorganic piezoelectric polyoxometalate-based subnanowire, ZnBiPMo12, which possesses intrinsic flexibility and chirality, a piezoelectric coefficient of 24.9 pC/N, and notable ferroelectricity. Leveraging its piezoelectric response, ZnBiPMo12-based PE-skin (1) demonstrates high elasticity and sensitivity to tiny pressures in the range of 0.045-0.319 N. Building on this, a wireless, wearable bioelectronic (WBE) device (1A) is fabricated through multi-level assembly, enabling non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals, including subtle muscle contractions, blinking, breathing, and all-day heart rate. By integrating a machine learning system, a 1-based facial-computer interface (1B) can accurately recognize nine emotional expressions and twelve spoken words. This work not only introduces a typical inorganic piezoelectric material with intrinsic flexibility but also demonstrates scalable manufacturing from subnanomaterials to wireless WBEs, paving the way for non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals and advanced human-computer interaction.

title: Improving the Calendar Life of Silicon Anodes with Inorganic Solid–Electrolyte Interphases
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Silicon anodes unlock higher energy density in Li-ion batteries but suffer from poor calendar life due to inadequately passivating solid–electrolyte interphases (SEIs). Here, we contrast the calendar aging behaviors of single- and mixed-salt locally superconcentrated electrolytes (LSCEs) against carbonate electrolytes. Mixed-salt LSCE cells retained 96% and 44% of precalendar capacity after one month and then after five months, while carbonate electrolyte cells retained 77% and 1%, respectively. The mixed-salt LSCE advantage is tied to the formation of a predominantly inorganic SEI, evidenced by nanoscale Fourier transform infrared spectromicroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and 3D time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry. After 5 months, however, perturbations to SEIs were evident in all cells, accelerating voltage decay and capacity loss by lithium inventory loss associated with SEI growth. These findings suggest that future electrolytes may benefit from strategies that continuously reinforce the SEI through controlled anion and solvent redox in LSCEs.

title: Formamidinium-Solvent Intermediates Mediate Self-Seeding Crystallization for Efficient Inverted α-FAPbI3 Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Formamidinium lead iodide (FAPbI3) perovskites are promising for high-performance solar cells; however, the low surface energy of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) impedes α-phase nucleation in inverted devices. Here, we report a formamidinium (FA)-solvent intermediate-mediated self-seeding crystallization strategy to enable quality α-phase FAPbI3. By employing N-formylmorpholine (NFM) as a non-toxic solvent, (FA···NFM)PbI3 intermediates are formed, thereby lowering the phase-transition barrier and promoting the spontaneous formation of α-phase nuclei at the early stage of crystallization. These preformed nuclei serve as intrinsic seeds, facilitating rapid nucleation and orientated crystal growth. Consequently, NFM-based devices achieve efficiencies of 26.41% and 26.56% using 2-methoxyethanol (2-Me) and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) as primary solvents, respectively, with a 1 cm2 device reaching 25.47%. The unencapsulated devices retain 85% and 90% of their initial efficiencies after 1200 h illumination and 1400 h thermal aging at 85 °C, respectively.

title: Electrochemical Control of Scholl Reaction: Arenium Cation Versus Radical Cation Pathways
abstract: ABSTRACT The Scholl reaction is a cornerstone method for constructing polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, yet its mechanism remains highly debated because arenium and radical cation intermediates are difficult to characterize. Herein, we demonstrate that electrochemical oxidation provides precise mechanistic control: a low‐potential acidic (LPA) condition selectively favors the arenium cation pathway, whereas a high‐potential neutral (HPN) condition promotes the radical cation pathway. While it is often assumed that only one mechanism operates under a given set of chemical oxidation conditions, our results reveal that most substrates can react via both pathways. Dialkoxyphenyl groups are found to facilitate the radical cation pathway, although no general correlation with overall substrate electron richness is observed. This electrochemical control provides the experimental basis to re‐evaluate previously proposed mechanisms for certain substrates. We demonstrate that switching between LPA and HPN conditions yields different products from the same 3,3’‐diphenyl‐2,2′‐binaphthalene substrate, thereby correcting the computational assignment of the corresponding pathways. Additionally, we show that a tetracene‐derived substrate undergoes cyclodehydrogenation through the arenium cation pathway, revising the computationally assigned dication mechanism for this transformation. Collectively, these results establish electrochemistry as a powerful alternative to traditional chemical oxidation, offering unprecedented experimental control to resolve fundamental mechanistic debates about the Scholl reaction.

title: Neutrophil Extracellular Trap‐Mimetic DNA Nets Enable Concurrent Bacteria‐Targeted Eradication and Toxin Neutralization
abstract: ABSTRACT Current antibacterial therapies often suffer from limited bacterial selectivity, host‐cell toxicity, and inflammation triggered by toxin release during bacterial killing. Here, we report a neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs)‐mimetic, dopamine‐incorporated DNA net, termed D A Net‐DA, enabling targeted bacterial eradication and concurrent toxin neutralization. Inspired by the trap‐kill‐neutralize function of NETs, D A Net‐DA selectively captures and traps bacteria, followed by in situ catalytic formation of polydopamine nanoshells on the trapped bacteria. This process enables efficient photothermal bacterial eradication while minimizing damage to host cells. Meanwhile, the nanoshells act as molecular sponges to sequester and neutralize bacterial toxins, thereby mitigating toxin‐associated inflammation. These integrated functions endow D A Net‐DA with potent therapeutic efficacy in vivo, as demonstrated by markedly reduced bacterial burdens, toxin levels, tissue inflammation in both conventional and burn wound infection models. Moreover, the simultaneous clearance of bacteria and residual toxins alleviates pro‐inflammatory macrophage polarization, thereby accelerating wound tissue regeneration. This work presents a NETs‐mimetic antibacterial strategy that integrates pathogen clearance with toxin neutralization, offering a promising method for treating bacterial infection‐associated diseases.

title: V─O─Ti Bridge‐Bond Polarity Boosts Na + Migration in V‐Based Fluorophosphates for Fast Sodium Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Vanadium‐based fluorophosphates are promising high‐energy‐density cathodes for next‐generation sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, the pronounced degradation of Na + diffusion at high voltage hinders their fast‐charging capability. Herein, a Ti 4+ ‐doping‐induced bridge‐bond‐polarity‐driven strategy is proposed to reshape the V electronic structure for facilitating V─O electron exchange. Correspondingly, voltage hysteresis, polarization, and structural distortion at high voltage are suppressed, accompanied by enhanced electronic conductivity. Meanwhile, the polar V─O─Ti bridge bonds expand the dominant one‐ and two‐dimensional Na + transport channels by inducing bridging‐O displacement, further boosting Na + migration capability. Therefore, Na 3 V 1.92 Ti 0.08 O(PO 4 ) 2 F 2 with V─O─Ti delivers high capacities of 121.8 and 62.1 mA h g −1 at 0.1C and 50C, respectively, while maintaining excellent cycling stability. Additionally, the 0.92‐Ah Na 3 V 1.92 Ti 0.08 O(PO 4 ) 2 F 2 //HC pouch cell exhibits 80% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 1C. At the 9 Ah scale, the pouch cell achieves a high energy density of 154 Wh kg −1 . This synergistic reinforcement strategy driven by bridge‐bond polarity paves the way for sustainable high‐power polyanionic SIBs.

title: Red Light‐Gated Charge Transfer Enables Trace Oxygen Response in Dye‐Sensitized TiO 2 –Carbon Nanotube Hybrids
abstract: ABSTRACT Light offers a powerful means of activating materials with spatial and temporal precision. However, translating excited‐state processes into chemically responsive electronic function in conductive solids remains challenging, particularly under low‐energy red illumination. Herein, we report red light‐gated charge transfer in dye‐sensitized single‐walled carbon nanotube–TiO 2 (SWCNT–TiO 2 ) hybrids that enables trace oxygen detection. Immobilization of red‐absorbing squaraine sensitizers on TiO 2 domains embedded within a conductive SWCNT network reversibly generates a photostationary charge‐transfer state under 628 nm excitation. Despite the low photon energy of red light, the hybrid architecture supports interfacial electron injection into TiO 2 and hole accumulation in the nanotube scaffold, while remaining electronically dormant in the dark. Interception of photogenerated electrons by O 2 perturbs this light‐induced state and converts excited‐state redox chemistry into a chemiresistive signal with ppb‐level sensitivity. This capability enables continuous monitoring of oxygen depletion in a sealed headspace during food spoilage. Electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, energy‐level alignment analysis, and charge‐carrier inversion experiments show that O 2 triggers light‐activated changes in SWCNT carrier density. These findings demonstrate that low‐energy optical excitation can gate chemical response in dye‐sensitized SWCNT–TiO 2 hybrids, establishing a design strategy for temporally controlled sensing and photoresponsive electronic function.

title: Resolving the Sensitivity–Specificity Trade‐Off in Fluorescent Probes via a Tandem‐Activatable Shielding Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT For precise tumor diagnosis, the intrinsic trade‐off between sensitivity and specificity in fluorescent probes remains a longstanding bottleneck, underscoring an urgent need for strategies to break this fundamental constraint. To address the specificity limitation, we exploited a highly polarity‐sensitive fluorescent scaffold to construct a tandem‐activatable probe, enabling sequential activation by the acidic tumor microenvironment and the angiogenic marker aminopeptidase N. Whereas the single‐locked counterpart is prone to premature activation in circulation, the tandem‐locked probe remains inactive owing to a maleamic acid‐based shielding unit and is activated only upon encountering these two tumor hallmarks. Furthermore, this shielding strategy increases probe hydrophobicity, enhancing tumor uptake and driving accumulation of released fluorophores in low‐polarity lipid droplets, where fluorescence is markedly amplified to improve imaging sensitivity. The probe exhibits rapid and specific activation across various solid tumors with minimal toxicity, thus effectively resolving the sensitivity‐specificity trade‐off in probe design for in vivo applications.

title: Extensive genomic diversity in Desulfovibrio reveals species-specific functional traits associated with disease
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Desulfovibrio spp. are associated with inflammatory diseases and human health, yet limited representative genomes and isolates hinder our understanding of their role in disease. Here, we assembled a comprehensive database of 2658 Desulfovibrio genomes across 90 diseases and 32 countries, including 24 human isolates. Genomic analyses showed extensive species diversity and revealed disease-associated functional traits, including flagellin and adaptation-associated genes (i.e., ureases). Flagellin-mediated Toll-like receptor 5 activation was species-specific and D. desulfuricans flagellin downregulated TGF-beta signalling in murine small intestinal organoids, suggesting impaired immune tolerance. Additionally, we investigated genomic capacity for hydrogen sulfide (H2S) production, a main Desulfovibrio metabolite. While health- and disease-associated Desulfovibrio spp. mainly encoded dissimilatory sulfate reduction, tetrathionate metabolism-encoding bacteria were exclusively detected in inflammatory bowel diseases, including Proteus mirabilis and Morganella morganii. Overall, our study provides a comprehensive genomic Desulfovibrio resource and identifies new links associating strain variation, functional traits and H2S-production with inflammatory diseases.

title: PRPF19 drives hepatic stellate cell activation and liver fibrosis via PKM2-mediated glycolytic reprogramming
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) is a pivotal event driving fibrogenic remodeling of the injured liver. However, the upstream regulators that integrate post-translational signaling with metabolic reprogramming during HSC activation remain poorly defined. Here, we identify pre-mRNA processing factor 19 (PRPF19) as a ubiquitination-linked metabolic regulator that promotes HSC activation. PRPF19 expression was elevated in human and murine fibrotic livers, enriched in activated HSCs, and positively correlated with fibrosis severity. Conditional deletion of Prpf19 in HSCs (Prpf19flox/flox;Lrat-CreERT2), but not in hepatocytes (Prpf19flox/flox;Alb-CreERT2), attenuated HSC activation and liver fibrosis in vivo. Integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses indicated that PRPF19 sustains glycolytic flux and transcriptional programs associated with HSC activation. Mechanistically, PRPF19 promoted K63-linked ubiquitination of pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2), facilitating its nuclear translocation and hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α)-dependent transcription of glycolytic and fibrogenic genes. These findings support a role for the PRPF19-PKM2 pathway in metabolic regulation during HSC activation and liver fibrosis.

title: Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis is concomitant with reduced metacognitive efficiency and sensitivity across multiple cohorts and modalities
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The corpus callosum is the largest commissure in the mammalian brain and has been implicated in supporting cognitive processes required for adapting to complex environments. Individuals born with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis, characterized by malformations of the corpus callosum, commonly exhibit deficits in social navigation, abstract problem-solving, decision-making, and self-awareness. Metacognition is a key cognitive process that supports these functions; however, it has yet to be tested comprehensively in individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis. Over three experiments, and three Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis cohorts, we examine perceptual accuracy, confidence judgments, and metacognitive efficiency in individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis using two variants of a Random Dot Kinematogram task within lab, online, and virtual reality conditions. We find that individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis typically display normal perceptual accuracy but fail to adjust their confidence judgments in line with task difficulty. Computational modeling reveal that this difference is characterized by lower metacognitive efficiency concomitant with lower metacognitive sensitivity. Together, these results provide evidence that the corpus callosum is consistently associated with reduced metacognitive efficiency.

title: Quantum-sensing-based super-resolution live cell microenvironment imaging
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Direct monitoring the multifaceted intracellular microenvironment is fundamental for deciphering localized cellular behavior and function. However, performing nanoscale spatiotemporal sensing of the dynamic physiochemical environment within a live cell has remained challenging, mainly limited by the lack of robust, biocompatible method which satisfies the requirements for spatiotemporal resolution, sensitivity, multi-physical sensing capability and long-term viability. Here we present a super-resolution-based quantum biosensing approach, namely Super-resolution Multi-physical field Imaging with Deconvolution, implemented in our custom-built setup which integrates nitrogen vacancy center-based quantum sensing with structured illumination microscopy. This enables quantitative, super-resolved, and long-term tracking of intracellular physical fields, featuring spatial resolution of 136 nm, temporal resolution of 150 ms, and field of view of 180×180 μm2. We further perform super-resolution multimodal imaging in a live cell, revealing the spatially heterogeneous reactive oxygen species dynamics under external stimulation. Our work enables the dynamic assessment of localized physiochemical dynamics under super-resolution quantum biosensing.

title: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda)
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The diversification of herbivorous dinosaurs and the rise of angiosperms in the Late Cretaceous are each well established, but the link between them is debated. Broad-scale diversity patterns in the two groups appear not to closely align, and there is no direct evidence of dinosaur adaptation to angiosperm-based diets. Here we describe Infernogallus jamesi gen. et. sp. nov., a diminutive caenagnathid oviraptorosaur, and show that these theropods were specialised herbivores that originated alongside the rise of fleshy angiosperm fruits. The nearly complete, articulated skull of Infernogallus jamesi—the first for the clade—reveals drastic changes to the adductor musculature organisation, unique in non-avian theropods but converged upon by extant frugivorous parrots. These modifications enabled extensive oral processing of soft food using anteroposterior movement of the mandible and occlusion of ridges and grooves on opposed elements. Altogether, this attests to a highly specialised herbivorous diet in caenagnathids, which likely consisted in large part of fleshy angiosperm fruits, which increased in size and diversity in concert with the radiation of oviraptorosaurs. Caenagnathids thus provide one of the strongest candidates for angiosperm-based diet adaptations in dinosaurs, but their role in the Late Cretaceous proliferation of fruit—which shaped early Cenozoic flora—remains unclear.

title: Somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decision bias via the superior colliculus
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Sensory inputs reach cortical and subcortical areas in parallel, but how they coordinate to guide decisions remains unknown. We examined the roles of the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) and the superior colliculus (SC) in mice performing whisker-mediated tactile detection. While inactivating S1 contralateral to the stimulus increased detection threshold, inactivating ipsilateral S1 decreased it. These opposing effects reflected shifts in choice bias rather than sensitivity. Unilateral SC inactivation produced similar directional effects, whereas bilateral inactivation of either S1 or SC neutralized bias. Furthermore, SC lesions impaired detection performance, and combined S1 inactivation caused no further impairment, indicating that S1-mediated shifts in bias were SC-dependent. S1 inactivation also decreased sensory-evoked neural activity in SC, and choice decoding revealed that behavioral impairment was more closely associated with changes in SC population activity than with loss of sensory encoding in S1. Thus, S1 shapes perceptual bias by modulating SC-dependent circuits that transform sensory evidence into perceptual decisions.

title: A self-limiting mechanotransduction feedback loop ensures robust organ formation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Organ morphogenesis uses mechanotransduction feedback loops to convert forces into gene expression changes that regulate cell mechanics. How these loops integrate with developmental programs to ensure robust outcomes remains unclear. We show that Yap mechanotransduction establishes a self-limiting positive feedback loop for semicircular canal formation in zebrafish. Canal development proceeds through bud initiation, extension, and fusion within the otic epithelium. Local swelling of hyaluronan-rich extracellular matrix (ECM) in the bud activates Yap in a spatial pattern. Yap increases the expression of its target, ccn1l1, promoting further ECM expansion to sustain bud extension. This feedback loop confers developmental robustness: graded ccn1l1 knockdown reduces extension rate, yet canal formation persists and fails only with strong disruption. Critically, the loop contains its own termination mechanism. During bud fusion, PKA signaling, activated by the adhesion GPCR Adgrg6, downregulates ccn1l1, ending the loop. These findings reveal how mechanotransduction loops with built-in termination provide developmental control by integrating mechanical forces, transcriptional responses, and morphogenetic outcomes.

title: CREST functions as a molecular bridge between neuron-specific enhancers and epigenetic regulators in mature motor neurons
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Motor neuron development requires precise transcriptional regulation mediated in part by BAF (BRG1/BRM-associated factor) chromatin remodeling complexes. The neuron-specific BAF subunit CREST is critical for neuronal function and is mutated in some cases of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), yet its underlying genomic mechanisms remain unclear. Using mouse embryonic stem cell differentiation, we show that CREST is essential for motor neuron maturation by activating mature neuronal genes and repressing progenitor genes. Mechanistically, CREST interacts with the neuronal transcription factors ONECUT1 and NGN2, and the BRM ATPase to target pre-existing accessible enhancers of neuronal genes. CREST deletion selectively prevents CBP histone acetyltransferase recruitment, reducing histone H3K27 acetylation at these enhancers and downregulating target gene expression, without disrupting BRM binding, enhancer accessibility, or long-range chromatin architecture. Overall, our findings identify CREST as a crucial epigenetic mediator bridging lineage-specific transcription factors, BAF complexes, and CBP to activate enhancers and promote proper motor neuron development.

title: Structural basis of ammonium transport and coordinated regulation of AMT1;1 in Arabidopsis thaliana
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Efficient ammonium uptake is essential for plant growth and nitrogen-use efficiency, yet the structural basis of ammonium transport and regulation in plant AMTs remains unclear. Here, we determined multiple cryo-electron microscopy structures of the Arabidopsis thaliana ammonium transporter AMT1;1 in apo, ammonium-bound, methylammonium-bound, low-pH and phosphomimetic states. These structures reveal a conserved ammonium conduction pathway comprising an aromatic recruitment vestibule, a Phe-gate/Twin-His-containing pore, and a polar intracellular exit region. We further identified a conserved extracellular N-terminal disulfide bond required for oligomer stability and transport activity, suggesting potential redox-dependent regulation. On the cytoplasmic side, phosphorylation modulates C-terminal interactions with intracellular loops, revealing an allosteric regulatory mechanism. Comparison with the bacterial ammonium-sensing protein Sd-Amt1 uncovers a conserved ammonium-recognition region in AtAMT1;1 that contributes to transport activity but lacks the signaling module and ligand-dependent conformational switching observed in Sd-Amt1. Together, these findings provide structural insight into ammonium transport and coordinated regulation in plant AMT transporters.

title: Transposable element-mediated structural variations shape gene expression and agronomic trait diversity in Brassica napus
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Brassica napus is a globally important allotetraploid oilseed crop with a complex genome and extensive structural diversity that remains incompletely characterized. Here, we present gap-free reference genome assemblies for Zhongshuang 11 (ZS11) and Westar, and assemble six additional accessions. We harmonize gene annotations across 22 genomes and develop BnaScope (https://rgmi.hzau.edu.cn/bnascope), a gene-centric functional genomics platform. Gene-based and graph-based pan-genomes identify 123,107 non-redundant gene clusters and 188,218 structural variants, including 112,417 transposable element-mediated structural variants (TEMSVs). TEMSVs show asymmetric distributions between An and Cn subgenomes and are associated with increased homoeolog expression imbalance, particularly for CDS-TEMSVs. SV-based genome-wide association analyses identify candidate genes underlying seed quality traits, and functional analyses demonstrate that BnaPYRDs negatively regulate seed glucosinolate content. These findings establish structural variation as an important contributor to homoeolog regulation and seed-quality variation in B. napus.

title: H3K27M cooperates with ASCL1 to maintain progenitor states and drive gliomagenesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Histone 3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitutions (H3K27M) drive aggressive diffuse midline gliomas by blocking differentiation of radial glial progenitor cells committed to oligodendrogenesis. We establish prolonged differentiation as a powerful tool to uncover regulators of glioma cell states and demonstrate that the pioneer transcription factor (TF) ASCL1 is a key mediator of H3K27M-driven plasticity and tumorigenesis. H3K27M prevents Polycomb silencing of ASCL1, co-opting this TF to maintain oligodendroglial progenitor states. Consistently, ASCL1 loss drastically impairs tumor formation in vivo. Mechanistically, ASCL1 synergizes with H3K27M to redistribute the chromatin remodeler BRG1 to regulatory elements co-enriched for ASCL1 and SOX motifs, promoting expression of stem and neural progenitor genes at the expense of mesenchymal genes in DMGs. ASCL1 loss acts as a “fire exit”, enabling alternative differentiation despite H3K27M, underscoring the therapeutic potential of targeting stalled differentiation and tumor plasticity in histone-mutant gliomas and cancers with a stem cell hierarchy.

title: Programming Hydrophobic Nanocavity of DNA Frameworks for Ultrastable Fluorescent Imaging
abstract: ABSTRACT Fluorescent proteins (FPs) are widely used in biological imaging, yet their limited programmability restricts adaptability for advanced nanoscale applications. Synthetic molecular containers offer designable cavities but struggle to simultaneously achieve large dimensions, biocompatible interfaces, and precise microenvironment control. Here we report DNA framework (DNF) dots, highly programmable fluorescent probes constructed by encapsulating Cy3 within three‐dimensional DNA‐encoded hydrophobic nanocavities. Using amphiphilic tetrahedral DNA frameworks with inward‐oriented alkyl chains, we create well‐defined nanocavities (4.8–8.9 nm) with tunable size, shape, and internal chemistry. Single‐molecule analysis reveals that DNF dots enhance photostability (up to 15‐fold) and total photon output (up to 58‐fold), as compared to single Cy3 tagged on single‐stranded DNA. The exceptional photostability and brightness of DNF dots enable stable binding event frequencies exceeding 7500 frames in DNA‐PAINT super‐resolution imaging. Furthermore, integration into light‐inducible DNA hydrogels yields rewritable information encoding platforms. DNF dots thus establish a versatile platform that combines the environmental shielding of fluorescent proteins with the programmability of synthetic molecular containers, introducing a DNA framework‐encoded microenvironment engineering paradigm for ultrastable fluorescent probes.

title: A dual-attribution framework reveals how foreign investment and trade redistribute cobalt availability
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Global resource allocation is increasingly shaped by foreign direct investment (FDI) and international trade, yet their combined effects on distribution of critical mineral availability across countries remain poorly quantified. Here, we develop a dual-attribution framework covering 193 countries and 36 territories that attributes primary cobalt availability according to corporate ownership and secondary availability according to international trade. We compare these estimates with a combined baseline scenario using geographic-production and pre-trade perspectives to assess how ownership and trade reshape country-level cobalt availability. Relative to this baseline, total cobalt availability is higher in 63.6% of countries, while 72.7% show a positive composite change when primary and secondary availability are equally weighted. Although these mechanisms do not alter the global total amount of cobalt available, they reduce its concentration across countries. Our findings highlight how FDI and trade reshape cobalt distribution and support resource-governance policies that account for both host and exporting countries.

title: Long-term nitrous acid evolution modulates ozone and secondary aerosol variations in global megacities
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nitrous acid (HONO) is a crucial urban source of HOx radicals, promoting surface ozone (O3) and secondary fine particle (PM2.5) formation, yet its long-term evolution and air-quality impacts remain poorly constrained. Here, using a deep neural network established on worldwide field campaigns, we reconstruct global surface HONO distributions. Typical megacities exhibited contrasting trends in 2005–2021, marked by a sharp decline in Beijing (−47.4% in 2013–2021), an increase in Delhi (+10.0% in 2005–2018), and slight decreases in London, New York and Los Angeles. These HONO changes are identified as major driver of O3 and particulate nitrate variations, outweighing contributions of conventional NOx and volatile organic compounds abatement in Beijing and Delhi, while showing comparable impacts in the remaining cities. A fused data-driven framework further uncovers regime-dependent HONO reduction strategies, prioritizing NOx control in summer and co-reduction of NOx, PM2.5 and direct combustion emissions in winter, to accelerate O3 and PM2.5 joint mitigation.

title: Fan Hong
Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mentalising, the ability to infer the beliefs and intentions of others, is essential for successful social interaction. Previous studies have implicated the medial prefrontal cortex in mentalising, but whether this region is necessary for higher-order mentalising remains unclear. Here we show that people with focal damage to the medial prefrontal cortex retain the ability to engage in higher-order mentalising during a strategic social game. We compare their performance with patients with brain damage in other regions and lesion-free participants. Individuals with medial prefrontal cortex damage achieve similar rewards and use comparable mentalising strategies, but they are slower when making strategic decisions. Computational modelling indicates that this slowing reflects a greater tendency to require evidence before committing to a choice. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identifies medial prefrontal regions linked to altered decision processes rather than mentalising. These findings suggest that the medial prefrontal cortex supports strategic decisions while higher-order mentalising remains intact.

title: Fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography using explicit neural fields
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Multimodal fluorescence and phase imaging provides complementary information about biological samples. However, existing simultaneous fluorescence-phase techniques primarily operate in transmission mode and are limited to thin specimens, restricting their use in thick tissues and in vivo applications. Although multiphoton microscopy enables deep-tissue fluorescence imaging, combining it with three-dimensional refractive-index (RI) imaging remains challenging because few methods can reconstruct the RI of bulky, label-free tissues in reflection mode at subcellular resolution. Here, we introduce fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography (FDT), which reconstructs the 3D RI of label-free and fluorescence-labeled objects from diffracted fluorescence images acquired in reflection mode under two-photon excitation. FDT uses the transport of intensity equation and a self-supervised neural network based on explicit neural fields. Compared with state-of-the-art implicit neural fields, this approach improves computational speed, reconstruction accuracy, and interpretability. We demonstrate FDT in two experimental regimes: reconstructing the 3D RI of label-free tissues up to 300 μm thick placed on a fluorescent substrate, and reconstructing the 3D RI of fluorescence-labeled, 3D-cultured cells without transmission-side access using fluorescence emitted by the cells themselves. FDT establishes a foundation for accessible reflection-mode multimodal fluorescence-phase imaging in complex biological systems.

title: Energy shocks, firm resilience, and policy responses: Evidence from the 2022 crisis*
Metal-organic frameworks for separation of organic compounds in liquid phase
abstract: Liquid-phase separation underpins numerous sectors of modern chemical industry, yet achieving high selectivity for separation of mixtures of organic compounds remains a persistent challenge. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), showing exceptional tunability in composition, topology and pore environment, hold unique promise to address this challenge. This review surveys recent progress in studies of MOFs for the selective extraction and purification of organic substrates in liquid phase, with a focus on elucidating the mechanism of selectivity. Function-directed design principles, encompassing tailored bonding interactions, programmable supramolecular environments and pore-confinement effects, are discussed as enabling precise control over transport processes. These concepts are examined across key application domains, including removal of pollutants in water treatment, the separation of structurally similar hydrocarbons in petrochemical refinery and the selective discrimination of daily pharmaceuticals. Opportunities for the next generation of MOF-based sorbents are outlined, highlighting challenges associated with scalability and long-term operational stability, and the growing roles of artificial intelligence (AI)-guided discovery in developing sustainable separation technologies are further projected.

title: Optimal inertia allocation in networked DC microgrids with guaranteed steady-state and small-signal stability
Coordinated planning and operation of SST-based DC data centers with tiered workload flexibility
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads is making modern data centers increasingly energy-intensive and reliability-critical. This trend not only raises electricity expenditure but also amplifies the economic impact of power interruptions, motivating coordinated planning of power infrastructure and computing resources. Against this background, solid-state transformer (SST)-based DC supply architectures are emerging as a promising direction for next-generation data centers because they provide a controllable interface for integrating diverse energy and computing resources. Under this architectural setting, this paper proposes a coordinated planning and operation framework for SST-based DC data centers with tiered workload flexibility. The framework incorporates nonlinear SST losses into long-term capacity planning, treats tiered workload flexibility as a planning resource, and coordinates energy storage and diesel generators for backup supply during utility outages. An annual bi-level model is formulated to jointly determine the capacities of SST conversion stages, renewable generation, energy storage, diesel generators, and heterogeneous computing servers, together with their scenario-dependent operating decisions. Piecewise linear approximation is used to reformulate the SST loss model, and an enhanced Benders decomposition algorithm is developed to solve the resulting multi-scenario mixed-integer problem. Case study results demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces total annual cost while satisfying workload service constraints. Further analysis shows that nonlinear SST losses influence capacity configuration, whereas tiered workload flexibility reshapes server deployment and backup resource requirements.

title: Ground-based spectral irradiance for intra-hour photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract: Electricity markets worldwide are shortening their settlement intervals, with Australia adopting 5-minute settlement in 2021 and the European Union now mandating a 15-minute imbalance settlement period across Member States. Shorter intervals sharpen the value of accurate intra-hour photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting at the timescale of cloud-induced ramp events, which broadband irradiance cannot fully resolve. In this study, ground-based high-resolution spectroradiometer measurements (213 channels, 350–1052 nm) are exploited as an input to short-horizon PV forecasting for the first time, and the gain is quantified across two climates and multiple years using data from the Solar Energy Research Institute of Singapore (SERIS). A SpectralEncoder is introduced, a lightweight 1-D convolutional network applied along the wavelength axis, combined with a physically motivated spectral-ratio representation that decouples spectral shape from broadband magnitude. Performance is evaluated under a dual-dimension framework crossing ramp/non-ramp conditions with clear/intermediate/overcast regimes defined by the clear-sky index. At the primary German site (temperate oceanic; trained 2018–2021, tested 2023), overall RMSE is reduced by 4.4% with spectral inputs, with the largest gain (+9.4%) under overcast ramp conditions, the regime most damaging to grid balancing. At the Australian site (hot desert; trained 2018–2020, tested 2022) the gain is 2.7%, of the same sign as at the German site. A noise-replacement control confirms the gain is driven by genuine spectral structure rather than dimensionality. The contribution is positively signed across forecast horizons from 15 to 90 min, holds across three model families (TCN, LSTM, LightGBM), and is statistically significant under day-block bootstrap ( p < 0.001 ). Post-hoc wavelength-importance analysis localises the signal to visible and near-infrared channels coinciding with known atmospheric absorption features, with cross-site Pearson correlation r = 0.69 . As market clearing intervals shrink and PV penetration rises, ground-based spectral irradiance, already collected at BSRN and collaborative PV testing networks worldwide, is a low-cost, deployable input feature for intra-hour forecasts.

title: Life cycle environment and direct operating cost assessment of coal to polyolefin integrated with coke oven gas, membrane separation and CO2 utilization
Regeneration-aware online SOH estimation framework for liquid metal batteries based on fragmented data
abstract: Liquid metal batteries (LMBs) are regarded as a promising candidate for grid energy storage, owing to their long lifespan and high safety. However, their accurate state of health (SOH) estimation is significantly hindered by the prevalence of fragmented data and the pronounced capacity regeneration phenomena observed during their high-temperature operation. To address these dual challenges, a hybrid modeling method that fuses physical prior knowledge with data-driven techniques is proposed. The framework is structured into two stages. In the first stage, to tackle data fragmentation, a curve reconstruction model based on a weak physics-informed neural network (W-PINN) augmented CNN-BiLSTM architecture is constructed. This model is capable of reconstructing complete LMB profiles from arbitrary sparse segments covering only 7% of the discharge range and remains robust under continuous and aging-biased data loss, effectively mitigating the physical distortion issues inherent in purely data-driven reconstruction models. In the second stage, to specifically address the capacity regeneration observed over the ultra-long lifecycle, a robust online SOH estimation strategy is developed. Based on the reconstructed curves, eight base health features are enhanced via canonical correlation analysis (CCA) and then processed by an online sequential extreme learning machine (OSELM) with prediction-based capacity-memory temporal features, enabling accurate SOH tracking under a strictly leak-free sequential inference protocol. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a reconstruction root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.0898 Ah and an SOH estimation RMSE of 0.1443% under fragmented input conditions with 20% reconstructed curves, exhibiting superior performance compared to existing baselines. Further evaluation on a 50 Ah LMB dataset validates the scalability of the complete two-stage framework, while the Oxford lithium-ion battery dataset provides supplementary evidence for the cross-chemistry adaptability of the Stage-1 reconstruction methodology. Ultimately, this work offers a practical and reliable solution for health monitoring of LMB-based energy storage systems (ESSs).

title: Unlocking the green power of the North Sea: Identifying key energy infrastructure synergies for 2030 and 2040
abstract: The North Sea will play a key role in providing clean and secure energy for Europe. This not only requires the development of new offshore wind farms, but also their successful integration into the onshore system. In this work we analyze and compare three key integration options and their preferred siting (onshore vs. offshore): grid expansions, electricity storage, and the production, storage and transport of low-carbon hydrogen. We focus on their potential to reduce emissions and energy system costs – individually and in combination with each other. Additionally, we study the consequences of constraints on their implementation. We analyze the years 2030 and 2040, starting from the projections of installed energy infrastructure and demand from the Ten Year Network Development Plan (TYNDP) 2022 of the European Network of Transmission System Operators (ENTSO-E). Results show that cross-border electricity grid expansions across the North Sea are a no-regret measure, resulting in significant reductions in system costs and emissions compared to national grid expansions. By comparison, the production, storage and transport of hydrogen have a lower cost and emission reduction potential. In both the short and long term (2030 and 2040), electricity storage can help to reduce emissions, but it is not cost competitive unless emission reduction targets are enforced. Combining the three integration measures at optimal capacities provides additional benefits. Overall, the highest emission reductions can be achieved by combining electricity storage with an expansion of the grid, while the highest economic benefits can be achieved with a combination of grid expansions and hydrogen production for direct use in industry.

title: Screening-based siting and metocean-aware O&M routing for floating offshore wind farms
Large-scale identical-location electron microscopy enables quantifying nanoparticulate electrocatalyst degradation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Fuel cells convert chemical energy into electricity, and their performance relies on electrocatalysts whose durability during operation remains poorly understood. Deep mechanistic insight into electrocatalyst stability is essential to design durable, resource-efficient fuel cells. Nanoparticulate electrocatalysts degrade via diverse nanoscale processes, yet particle-to-particle heterogeneity in structure, support interaction, and local microenvironment make true particle-level quantification and understanding impossible with classical approaches. Here we scale up identical-location scanning transmission electron microscopy, which repeatedly images the very same nanoparticles, to track the structural evolution of hundreds of carbon-supported platinum-cobalt nanoparticles, a prototypical oxygen reduction reaction electrocatalyst. We present a three-step image analysis workflow comprising segmentation, tracking, and degradation-event classification with progressive automation, including machine-learning-assisted detection of overlapping particles. By pairing nanoscale resolution and local history with population-level statistics, the pipeline enables unbiased identification and quantification of degradation pathways across statistically meaningful particle sets. We reveal particle size- and shape-dependent effects, showing that smaller and irregular nanoparticles are more prone to detachment, and provide a data-driven framework for probing electrocatalyst degradation at scale.

title: Beyond nature: charting the roadmap to intelligent biomanufacturing for sustainable biohydrogen
abstract: Hydrogen has been recognized as a key pillar of future energy systems in the global pursuit of carbon neutrality. However, hydrogen production processes still highly rely on fossil fuels. Biohydrogen production is a microbial-based process that converts biomass, organic waste, and solar energy into hydrogen via dark fermentation, photo-fermentation, or photolytic water-splitting pathways. It is a promising pathway to sustainable energy, with the potential for carbon-negative emissions under favorable feedstock and system-boundary conditions. Yet, the limitations of natural biological systems, such as poor energy conversion efficiency, huge carbon diversion, and poor operational robustness, have prevented its transition from laboratory research to industrial application. To resolve these bottlenecks, this review proposes a strategic shift from traditional biological conversion toward intelligent biomanufacturing via three enabling technologies: (1) synthetic biology to design microbial cell factories with a tailored hydrogen-centric metabolism; (2) nanomaterials engineering to create smart biotic-abiotic interfaces for overcoming the physical limitations of electron and mass transfer; and (3) artificial intelligence to enable autonomous bioprocessing through predictive digital twins and self-optimizing reactor systems. These three pillars can bridge molecular-scale engineering to system-level intelligence. A scalable roadmap starting from modular bioreactor design, waste-derived feedstock integration, and rigorous techno-economic and life-cycle assessment has been outlined to position biohydrogen within circular economy and potentially carbon-negative ecosystems. This review suggests a pathway to make biohydrogen an important, efficient, cost-effective, and reliable building block of the future hydrogen economy.

title: Advances in self-reconstructing stainless-steel electrocatalysts for water splitting: surface activation, alloy engineering, stability, and DFT insights
abstract: Stainless steel (SS) is emerging as a promising, earth-abundant platform for replacing precious-metal and pure-Ni electrodes in water electrolysis. Yet, it is still often treated as inert hardware rather than an active catalyst. Under HER/OER conditions, however, the classical Cr-rich passive film on Fe-Cr-Ni alloy SS is driven beyond its stability window. It can reconstruct into porous, Ni/Fe-rich (oxy)hydroxide layers that provide genuine catalytic activity while remaining anchored to a robust metallic backbone. This review consolidates evidence on how such self-reconstruction can be intentionally controlled and engineered to convert commercial SS into efficient, durable electrodes for overall water splitting. We first summarize the evolution of SS from a structural material to a self-reconstructing electrocatalyst, and critically discuss surface-activation strategies, including electrochemical activation (potential cycling, anodization, and cathodization), thermal oxidation, and hydrothermal/corrosion-engineering routes that drive Cr depletion and Ni/Fe enrichment. We then introduce the Ni-Fe-Cr-X reservoir concept to bridge the gap between traditional corrosion science and modern electrocatalysis, rationalizing how bulk alloy composition and microstructure govern reconstruction behavior, secondary passivation, and stability across alkaline and chloride-containing environments. Emphasis is placed on long-term durability, including self-replenishing Ni-rich electrodes that operate at ampere-level current densities, and on the limited but growing density functional theory (DFT) literature that links passive-film chemistry and electronic structure to HER/OER mechanisms. Finally, we outline key research directions, including multi-scale operando characterization, composition-designed SS, and specific DFT/ML frameworks needed to move from empirical activation toward rational, mechanism-guided design of SS-based electrocatalysts.

title: NMR Spectroscopic Evidence for Magnetically Induced Ring Currents in All-Metal-Aromatic [Bi4]4+
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Experimental assignment of aromaticity in all-metal systems remains challenging, particularly for heavy-element clusters, where local magnetic effects can obscure signatures of circular electron delocalization. Here, we investigate a supramolecularly stabilized, formally tetracationic [Bi4]4+ ring by combining structurally meaningful reference compounds, solid- and solution-state NMR spectroscopy, SQUID magnetometry, and exact two-component relativistic calculations. Comparison with an isostructural [Li4Br]3+-encapsulated analogue and a binuclear Bi(III) reference compound disentangles global ring-current effects from local heavy-atom deshielding and ligand-specific conformational effects. On this basis, the unusually downfield-shifted 1H and 13C NMR signals observed for the Bi4-containing species provide direct spectroscopic evidence for magnetically induced ring currents in the [Bi4]4+ core. By contrast, bulk magnetic measurements do not reveal significant diamagnetic exaltation, indicating that this quantity is not a resolved descriptor of aromaticity in these systems. Stoichiometric studies further identify chemically competent intermediates that provide mechanistic snapshots of [Bi4]4+ ring formation. Complementary calculations support the assignment of a magnetically responsive, σ-delocalized [Bi4]4+ core, reproduce a rare spectroscopically observed puckering motion of the rhomboidal [Bi4]4+, and underscore the critical role of spin–orbit coupling on electronic structure and dynamics. Overall, this work moves the discussion of aromaticity from predominantly computational assignment toward experimentally benchmarked analysis in the heavy-element and all-metal regime.

title: Metal Fluorides: All-In-One Supports for Ruthenium-Catalyzed Ammonia Synthesis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ammonia, an emerging energy carrier, demands advanced catalysts for synthesis under mild conditions to integrate with green hydrogen. We herein establish a family of metal fluoride supports (MFn, M = Li, Na, K, Mg, Ca, or Ba) as a tunable “all-in-one” platform for ruthenium (Ru) catalysts. These Ru/MFn systems unify the critical merits of various existing catalysts, such as support-mediated activation of reactants and air stability. Varying the host cation can direct the catalytic pathway. Consequently, Ru/NaF exhibits excellent turnover frequency, while Ru/BaF2 delivers an NH3 synthesis rate of 58.0 mmolNH3 gcat–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 0.9 MPa─surpassing all reported Ru-based catalysts with ≤4 wt % Ru and without external promoters. Advanced characterization reveals that the fluorine vacancy formation energies of the alkali and alkaline-earth lattices, together with the vacancy-reactant interactions, dictate the divergent catalytic mechanisms mediated by different active sites. This work expands the chemistry of metal fluorides, launching a new paradigm for potentially viable NH3-synthesis under mild conditions.

title: Regio- and Enantioselective Functionalization of Gaseous Alkanes via Nickel-Catalyzed Alkene Dicarbofunctionalization
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The regio- and enantioselective functionalization of gaseous alkanes remains an unsolved challenge in organic synthesis. Here, we report a general strategy for the asymmetric three-component dicarbofunctionalization of alkenes using readily available gaseous alkanes, including ethane, propane, and isobutane. This transformation, enabled by the merger of hydrogen atom transfer photocatalysis with a chiral nickel catalyst, efficiently delivers chiral α-aryl carbonyl compounds in good yield with excellent regio- and enantioselectivity (up to >20:1 rr and 99:1 er). Experimental and computational studies reveal insights into the mechanism controlling selectivity. Operating under exceptionally mild, energy-efficient conditions, the method unlocks a versatile platform for upgrading feedstock gaseous alkanes into sought-after chiral building blocks.

title: Hydrogenation of CO2 to Propane and n -Butane by Engineering Metal Oxide Interfacial Structure and Manipulating Zeolite Pore Structure and Acidity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Selective hydrogenation of CO2 to propane and n-butane is of great interest, as these two compounds are not only primary components of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) but also crucial raw materials for preparing propene and a degradable plastic precursor of succinic acid. Although various composite catalysts combining metal oxides and zeolites have been explored, their catalytic performances remain insufficient. Here, we found that ZnZrOx decorated with ultrasmall FeOx clusters, forming an intimate FeOx–ZnZrOx interfacial structure, showed high catalytic activity for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol due to a strong CO2 adsorption capacity and H2 dissociation ability, and silicoaluminophosphate molecular sieve with RHO topological structure enhanced methanol conversion into propane and n-butane via hexamethylbenzenes as active hydrocarbon pool species owing to its unique supercage structure and double eight-membered ring pore opening. As a result, coupling of these two materials delivers a CO2 conversion of ∼66% and a (propane + n-butane) selectivity of 82% in hydrocarbons, which leads to a (propane + n-butane) yield of ∼42%. It is surprising that this composite preferentially produces n-butane rather than iso-butane, and the n-butane/iso-butane ratio is higher than 85.8. The high catalytic stability of this composite is demonstrated by maintaining CO2 conversion, (propane + n-butane) selectivity in hydrocarbons, and their yield of ∼ 61%, ∼ 77%, and ∼ 31%, respectively, after a reaction of 620 h. This work not only fabricates a high-performance catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation to propane and n-butane by engineering the metal oxide interfacial structure and manipulating the zeolite’s pore structure and acidity, but also makes it possible to develop an efficient way for preparing propene and succinic acid from CO2 hydrogenation.

title: Electroanalytical and Computational Investigation of Oxoammonium-Mediated Hydride Transfer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Oxoammonium-mediated hydride transfer is an important yet relatively underexplored elementary step in C–H functionalization. In this work, we employed cyclic voltammetry (CV) to measure the rates of hydride transfer between electrochemically generated oxoammonium catalysts and 42 substrates including ethers, carbamates, amides, and sulfonamides. Through quantum mechanical (QM) calculations, we uncovered a new transition-state model for hydride transfer in which the N atom of the catalyst resides near a heteroatom (X = N or O) of the substrate to allow alignment of the oxoammonium’s O═N+ motif and the substrate’s forming C═X+ bond. Energy decomposition analysis was subsequently performed to elucidate the key factors that govern the kinetics of oxoammonium-mediated hydride transfer. Beyond conventional electronic and steric considerations, we identified substrate distortion, secondary orbital interactions, and noncovalent interactions as critical factors that influence hydride transfer reactivity. We anticipate that these kinetic data along with the mechanistic insights they provide will inform future catalyst development and synthetic applications to broaden the scope of oxoammonium catalysis.

title: Selective Consecutive Decarboxylation Enables Skeletal Contraction of Waste PET
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Direct catalytic upcycling of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) to benzene through consecutive decarboxylation contracts the terephthalate-derived C8 framework to C6, representing a skeletal-editing strategy for aromatic polycarboxylates. The key challenge is to control pathway selection across consecutive decarboxylation steps, favoring sequential aryl–carboxyl C–C bond cleavage over competing hydrogenolysis while preserving the aromatic core. Herein, we report an efficient direct catalytic conversion of waste PET to benzene, achieving an exceptionally high yield of 83.3% over a tailored Ru/W0.4ZrOx catalyst. The performance arises from synergistic acid-site reconstruction and oxygen-vacancy engineering. Moderate WOx incorporation into ZrO2 converts Lewis acidity into Brønsted acidity, while oxygen vacancies and WOx species promote adsorption and activation of carboxyl groups. In cooperation with Ru nanoparticles, these features preferentially stabilize the decarboxylation intermediate over its hydrogenolysis counterpart, directing both consecutive steps toward C–C bond cleavage while suppressing undesired hydrogenolysis pathways. Controlled hydrogen supply and a deliberately designed dodecane/water mixed solvent system further enhance selectivity. The catalyst performs effectively across diverse real-world PET wastes, with preliminary techno-economic and life-cycle analyses indicating favorable process-level metrics under the evaluated assumptions. More broadly, these mechanistic insights establish synergistic acidity and oxygen-vacancy regulation as a catalyst-design principle for decarboxylative skeletal editing of aromatic polycarboxylates.

title: Engineering a Reconfigurable Transmembrane Receptor Enables Logic-Controlled Signal Translocation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Transmembrane receptors relay extracellular cues into intracellular responses through reconfigurable conformational changes, yet engineering synthetic systems that emulate receptor-like signal translocation with programmable control remains challenging. Here, we engineer a reconfigurable transmembrane receptor that enables logic-controlled signal translocation across lipid membranes. The receptor is constructed from an oriented Y-shaped triplex DNA architecture that inserts directionally into the plasma membrane via dual cholesterol anchors and integrates two environmental inputs─H+ and ATP─through an i-motif and an aptamer module. Under dual-input conditions, cooperative duplex-to-triplex switching triggers reconfigurable structural rearrangement and drives transmembrane relocation of a signaling strand from the outer to the inner membrane leaflet. This receptor-mediated signal translocation converts extracellular chemical cues into spatially defined intracellular activation. The repositioned strand serves as a modular intracellular effector that can be functionalized to implement programmable reactions, including bioorthogonal catalysis and light-triggered photocatalysis at the membrane interface. Importantly, endogenous tumor-microenvironmental cues trigger receptor reconfiguration and signal translocation in 3D tumor spheroids and in vivo, enabling logic-gated intracellular photocatalysis and >85% tumor growth inhibition in xenograft models. By coupling logic-gated reconfigurable switching with directional transmembrane signal propagation, this work establishes an engineered transmembrane receptor for programmable intracellular activation and provides a general strategy for synthetic signal translocation in living systems.

title: Deciphering Interheme Electron-Transfer Pathways in a Diheme Peroxidase from Methane-Oxidizing Bacteria
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bis-FeIV-forming enzymes represent an emerging paradigm in high-valent heme iron chemistry, in which two hemes separated by 15–20 Å are both oxidized to the FeIV state. A tryptophan positioned between the two hemes in two out of the three known enzymes to form this state, MauG and MbnH, has been proposed as the dominant pathway for interheme electron transfer. .The third enzyme, BthA, instead has a serine at this position. Here, we used site-directed mutagenesis of Trp113 in MbnH to test whether this tryptophan is uniquely required for interheme electron transfer. Computational pathway analysis identified the possibility of an alternative, noncovalent route mediated by Arg283 and a heme propionate with possible electronic coupling comparable to that of the native tryptophan pathway. Consistent with this prediction, only simultaneous disruption of both the tryptophan and propionate-mediated pathways abolished bis-FeIV formation entirely. Moreover, only mutants capable of forming bis-FeIV retained the ability to turnover substrate, directly establishing this high-valent state as the catalytic intermediate responsible for substrate modification. These results demonstrate that an intervening tryptophan is not required for fast interheme electron transfer, and instead reveal an additional, noncovalent pathway that may be a general feature of diheme peroxidases.

title: Birch-Type-Reduced Carbazole Anions Enable Redox-Adaptive Super-Reducing Photocatalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic activation of inert chemical bonds is constrained by the redox potential of the catalyst. Here, we report a redox-adaptive photocatalytic strategy in which an electron-rich carbazole photocatalyst, CBZ6, functions as a molecular redox transformer through the formation of Birch-type carbazole anions. Under visible light, CBZ6 switches between a neutral state for conventional photoredox reactions and an anionic state for super-reducing catalysis. Excitation of the anionic state generates a super-reducing species with an excited-state oxidation potential of approximately −3.6 V versus SCE, substantially beyond that of the neutral excited state (−2.2 V). This adaptive redox switching enables activation of otherwise inaccessible C–F bonds in aryl fluorides, polyfluoroalkyl compounds, and fluoropolymers. The complementary reactivities of the two states further enable diverse photoredox transformations, establishing redox adaptation as a strategy for expanding the accessible reactivity of organic photocatalysts.

title: Cesium-Induced Stabilization of the FeOOH Cocatalyst on Bismuth Vanadate Photoanode for Ultraefficient and Stable Photoelectrochemical Water Oxidation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing active and durable water oxidation cocatalysts is essential for advancing photoelectrochemical (PEC) water-splitting systems. This study investigates the cesium-induced reconstruction of the FeOOH cocatalyst on a bismuth vanadate (BVO) photoanode for the water oxidation reaction, with a focus on the reconstruction process and its effect in improving interfacial charge transfer and photostability. Cesium ions induce the reconstruction of Fe species on the BVO/FeOOH photoanode during the PEC process, leading to the formation of a robust Cs-incorporated FeOOH (Cs:FeOOH) catalytic layer. Spectroscopic analysis combined with open-circuit potential measurement reveals that the in situ formed Cs:FeOOH cocatalyst can effectively protect BVO and promote interfacial hole transfer during PEC operation. As a result, the BVO/Cs:FeOOH photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 6.29 mA cm–2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE and maintains stable operation for over 100 h. Furthermore, the Cs-incorporated FeOOH cocatalyst strategy can be extended to other semiconductor systems, including TiO2 and FeOx, highlighting its broader potential for improving solar-driven PEC water oxidation.

title: Circular RNA Delivery In Vitro and In Vivo Using Doubly Branched Aminoethoxy-Functionalized Ionizable Lipid Nanoparticles
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Circular RNA is a therapeutically promising RNA modality with superior stability and extended protein expression relative to linear RNA. While delivery systems for linear RNA have received much attention, less effort has been directed toward the delivery of circular RNA, whose closed topology and physicochemical properties differ from those of linear RNAs. Here, we disclose a class of ionizable lipids that enable efficient in vitro and in vivo delivery of circular RNA. These ionizable lipids are step-economically accessible, allowing facile assessment of their structure–delivery relationships. Our studies reveal key elements that enhance circular RNA delivery in vitro and in vivo, including aminoethoxy head units, doubly branched tails and linkers tuned for hydrogen bonding and biodegradability. The lead ionizable lipid for circular RNA delivery, iL-19, incorporating these features, achieves ∼28-fold higher protein expression in C2C12 myocytes than Moderna’s SM-102 formulation and 2.5-fold higher expression upon intramuscular administration in BALB/c mice. iL-19 also surpasses benchmark ionizable lipids ALC-0315 (7.8-fold) and DLin-MC3-DMA (33.4-fold) for intramuscular circular RNA delivery in vivo under otherwise identical conditions. This study establishes design principles and a step-economical synthesis for accessing ionizable lipids that enable highly efficient in vitro and in vivo circular RNA delivery.

title: Grid integration of bidirectional dynamic wireless charging for electric vehicles: A review on grid-side challenges and opportunities
Passive anti-frosting strategies based on interfacial humidity regulation: From mechanisms to applications
abstract: Frost formation in low-temperature environments causes significant efficiency losses and safety hazards across aerospace, HVAC, and manufacturing industries. Conventional active anti-frosting methods suffer from poor energy efficiency due to periodic energy input requirements. This review summarizes recent advances in passive anti-frosting through interfacial humidity regulation—a strategy that inhibits ice crystal nucleation and growth by actively controlling local water vapor, offering substantial energy-saving potential. We firstly discuss theoretical models of ice nucleation in supersaturated vapor, examining how surface energy, microstructure, and chemistry govern interfacial humidity distribution and phase transitions. Secondly, three widely reported humidity regulating media, ice, hygroscopic gels, and hygroscopic liquids, are examined in terms of their vapor regulation mechanisms and frost suppression performance. Thirdly, we address advanced anti-frosting strategies based on interfacial humidity regulation via hygroscopic materials, biological protein and inspired microstructured surfaces. This review provides theoretical foundations and technical guidance for next-generation energy-efficient frost suppression technologies.

title: A comprehensive review on accurate numerical simulation of proton exchange membrane fuel cell
abstract: PEMFCs involve strongly coupled electrochemical reactions and transport processes of gas, water, charge, and heat. Numerical simulation is therefore an important tool for understanding internal transport phenomena, predicting performance, and supporting PEMFC design and operation. This structured narrative review synthesizes representative PEMFC numerical-simulation studies identified primarily through topic-specific manual searches of the Web of Science database. While many earlier reviews focus on individual processes, components, scales, or modeling routes, the present review connects numerical models from the MEA to macro-scale and multi-scale single-cell models, stack models, operational-process models, system temperature-control models, and efficient-study models based on artificial intelligence and similarity theory. The principal modeling approaches are compared in terms of their physical descriptions, applicable scales, computational costs, validation approaches, and suitable applications. The review shows multi-physics and multiscale models are essential for resolving coupled internal processes, but their effectiveness is constrained by uncertain transport and kinetic parameters, coupling methodology between scales, limited validation data for local physical fields, and high computational cost for large stacks. AI-assisted and reduced-order approaches can improve computational efficiency, but their prediction capability and applicable scale require further development. The review provides a structured summary and outlooks for selecting and improving PEMFC numerical models.

title: Exploring R˜2 Leptoquarks and Majorana Neutrinos via same-sign dimuons at the HL-LHC
abstract: Publication date: Available online 10 October 2026Source: Physics Letters BAuthor(s): Subham Saha, Arvind Bhaskar, Manimala Mitra

title: Energy transition and corporate geographic expansion
Carbon pricing and clean energy markets: Policy effectiveness in an era of trade wars
Energy transition under fragmentation: A threshold analysis of inclusive governance in developing economies
abstract: Although institutional quality is widely recognised as important for environmental performance, less is known about whether the governance–energy relationship varies across levels of institutional capacity. This study examines the relationship between inclusive governance, energy intensity, and CO 2 emissions volatility across 71 developing economies in the context of an increasingly fragmented global energy system. We focus on whether the governance–energy relationship varies across levels of institutional capacity. Inclusive governance is measured using a composite index incorporating political institutional quality, gender representation, and income equality. The empirical analysis uses a piecewise panel specification based on the sample median of inclusive governance, with system-GMM and local-projection estimates providing supplementary sensitivity evidence. Inclusive governance is negatively and significantly associated with energy intensity in both governance regimes in the baseline specification, with a somewhat stronger association in the higher-governance regime. However, this nonlinear pattern is sensitive to alternative estimators and breakpoints and is therefore interpreted as suggestive rather than definitive. In contrast, inclusive governance is not significantly associated with CO 2 emissions volatility across most specifications. These findings indicate that the relationship between governance and environmental performance may be outcome-specific: institutional capacity is more clearly associated with energy efficiency than with emissions volatility. The results are interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal effects and suggest that the environmental relevance of governance may vary with both institutional capacity and the outcome being examined.

title: Catalysts or constraints? The dual role of natural resources and greenfield investment amid geopolitical risk
Exploiting dynamics of electricity–hydrogen–carbon markets using adaptive operating rules for hybrid energy systems
abstract: Electricity markets have traditionally shaped the operating strategies of hybrid energy systems (HESs) integrating hydropower, wind, and photovoltaic resources. Meanwhile, the rapid emergence of hydrogen and carbon markets is transforming system operation by linking electricity supply, hydrogen production, and carbon-related revenues. However, existing electricity–hydrogen operating rules do not account for how pathway-dependent carbon values alter the allocation of renewable electricity between grid delivery and hydrogen production. This study embeds pathway-dependent carbon valuation into the shared energy-allocation decision, allowing the carbon signal to reshape the relative benefits of grid delivery and hydrogen production and propagate into hybrid system operation and operating-rule parameters. An operation-mediated price-feedback framework is incorporated into the long-term operation model to maximize operating benefit and supply assurance. The optimized results are then synthesized into adaptive operating rules through a parameterization–simulation–optimization framework. A case study of the Ertan hydro–hydrogen–wind–photovoltaic system shows that the reservoir release is the key decision variable in rule formulation. The derived optimal operating rules achieve 616.03 million USD in operating benefit and a 98.96% assurance rate, improving conventional rules by 14.94% and 10.79%. These results demonstrate that adaptive operating rules can effectively exploit electricity–hydrogen–carbon market dynamics, thereby enhancing the energy use efficiency of HESs.

title: Decarbonization dispatch for AI computing center parks considering task-level carbon traceability
abstract: The decarbonization dispatch of AI computing centers should not stop at controlling total park-level carbon emissions; it should also trace the energy sources, carbon-emission responsibility, and low-carbon labels of individual AI tasks. To address the limitation that existing studies mainly adopt park-average accounting and therefore cannot support task-level accounting, this paper proposes a decarbonization dispatch optimization method for AI computing center parks considering task-level carbon traceability.
